claim: The Malay Basin is a Cenozoic rift basin located in the southern part of the South China Sea, formed during late Eocene/Oligocene extension.
Group D, E, and F reservoirs are primarily fluvial-deltaic sandstones with high porosity (15-25%) and permeability.
Fault seal risk is high for Group I reservoirs due to shale gouge ratio (SGR) variability under high fault displacement.
A Class III AVO anomaly in the deep syn-rift Group M sandstones represents a high-saturation gas reservoir.
Malay Basin is offshore east of Peninsular Malaysia and contributes about 40% of Malaysia’s hydrocarbon resources in the review period.
Exploration history shows mature-basin creaming behavior: early giant discoveries, later smaller incremental additions.
Malay Basin initiated by Late Eocene–Early Oligocene extension, high post-rift subsidence, >14 km sediment in deepest centre, E-W half-grabens influenced by Pre-Tertiary faults.
Stratigraphy uses groups A–P; drilling reaches at least Group M; fill transitions from lacustrine/non-marine to coastal plain and shallow marine; K shale marks key transition.
Main resources are reported from Groups J, I, K, E, D; I/J/K contribute about 60%, and D/E plus those contribute about 85%; deltaic sands dominate.
Oils/condensates derive mainly from lower coastal plain fluvio-deltaic coal/coaly shale and lacustrine syn-rift shales; northwest is gas-prone, southeast more oil-prone.
Remaining potential is not zero; paper estimates roughly 2 bboe yet to discover by 2020, but requires new play concepts.

Malay Basin stratigraphy includes Groups A, B, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M (Group C absent — EPMI nomenclature). Group G is a marine-influenced transition unit between F and H. Group L is a regional seal for basin flank overpressure and the best lacustrine source rock.
source: Madon 2004, Madon 2010 GSM, Knova UM 2020, USGS OF99-50-T

claim: Group K is BOTH a fluvial reservoir (~16% of reserves) AND a lacustrine source rock (K-Source Facies, TOC 0.35-2.0 wt%, HI 137-403 with mixed Type II/III). Group L is best source (HI 300-400, lacustrine).
source: Madon 2010 GSM Bulletin — Organic facies variation in lacustrine source rocks

claim: Two overpressure compartments in Malay Basin: (1) Basin centre — top of OP at 1900-2000m in lower Group E, sealed by Group F shale, deeper compartment extends through Groups K, L, M; (2) Basin flank — top of OP at 2600-3000m, sealed by Group L shale.
source: Madon 2004 SPE 88455 — Overpressure History of Malay Basin
